Subject: VoiceOver accessibility issues in Telegram for iOS

Hello Telegram team,

I'm a VoiceOver user, and I'd like to report that Telegram for iOS still has significant accessibility problems. Some buttons and interface elements are unlabeled or are not read aloud, and the navigation order is sometimes confusing. This makes everyday tasks like browsing chats, opening settings, and sending messages and files difficult.

I always keep the app up to date, and I'm currently running the latest version available. Unfortunately, every time a new version comes out and I update, I end up disappointed, because these problems are still there. A number of other users have also reported similar issues on bugs.telegram.org over the past few years, and some are still reproducible in recent versions.

Many blind and low-vision people rely on Telegram to stay in touch with family, friends, and communities. Could you please prioritize VoiceOver support by labeling all interactive elements, keeping the focus order logical, and testing each release with VoiceOver before it ships?

Device: iPhone 17
iOS version: iOS 27.3 beta
Telegram version: Latest version available on the App Store ([version number])

Thank you very much for your time and for your work on Telegram.

Best regards,

reviews.title: Urgent Bug Report: Keyboard Not Dismissing & Performance Issues on iPhone 6s (iOS 15.8.8)
reviews.text:
Dear Telegram Development Team,
I hope this message finds you well. Thank you for your continuous work on the app.
I am writing to report several critical issues I am experiencing on my iPhone 6s running iOS 15.8.8. With the recent updates, the app has become increasingly difficult to use on this older hardware. I would like to bring the following issues to your attention:
.1 Keyboard Bug (Most Critical): When I try to swipe the keyboard down to dismiss it, it does not close and remains stuck on the screen. It stays open and blocks a significant portion of the chat interface. I have attached a screenshot to demonstrate this exact issue. Please see how the keyboard remains fully visible and cannot be dismissed.
.2 Performance: The app has become noticeably slower. The device seems unable to handle the processing load of the recent changes, making basic navigation and typing laggy.
.3 Unexplained Crashes: The app occasionally crashes for no apparent reason, even during normal use. 
I understand that supporting older devices can be challenging, but the iPhone 6s and iOS 15 are still widely used. I kindly request that your team look into these issues, particularly the keyboard dismissal bug, so that users on older but functional devices can continue to use Telegram smoothly.
Thank you for your time and for your continued efforts. I look forward to a fix in a future update.
Best regards
Device: iPhone 6s | iOS: 15.8.8 | Telegram

reviews.title: Weak privacy!
reviews.text:
Telegram has a serious doxxing and privacy problem. Its current design makes it far too easy to use OSINT techniques to connect information scattered across public groups, channels, shared links, usernames, profile photos, and other publicly accessible content. A single message containing a link can potentially become a starting point for identifying a user’s other accounts and online activity, especially when old messages remain accessible.

The problem is not simply that users share information publicly; it is that Telegram provides very few safeguards against someone systematically aggregating those fragments into a detailed profile of an individual, potentially exposing highly sensitive personal information.

For a platform that markets itself around privacy, this is unacceptable. Telegram needs stronger anti-doxxing protections, better control over the discoverability and persistence of user-generated content, and clearer privacy defaults.

This issue is particularly frustrating because I have to attend 2–3 hour-long lectures on Telegram, and without a working progress bar and forward option, it is extremely difficult to watch them.

I request the Telegram team to please investigate this issue and fix it as soon as possible.

Thank you for your support and cooperation.

reviews.title: Worst app management for Critical Storage Leak on iOS/iPadOS
reviews.text:
This app has a severe bug where clearing the cache from within the app settings does not actually free up any device storage. Even if you limit the cache size or manually hit “Clear Entire Cache,” Telegram continues hoarding gigabytes of data in the system storage as “Documents & Data,” leaving the device completely bloated and unresponsive.
The storage usage graph in the app claims space was freed, but checking iPhone/iPad Storage settings shows the exact same bloat. The only temporary workaround is entirely deleting the app and reinstalling it, which is unacceptable for a messaging app. Please fix this massive storage leak immediately; it has been a known issue for far too long.

reviews.title: Won’t fix bugs any more
reviews.text:
I’ve used Telegram for over a decade now. It used to be awesome. Unfortunately, in the past few years, their priorities have changed. Their definition of “the best messenger” is “the one with the most features.” In order to achieve this, Telegram has stopped fixing bugs in the existing features.

Now, everything in the app is half-baked, and they’re starting to smear useless GenAI features on top of all the other stuff that doesn’t work. I didn’t want the passport feature. I didn’t want stories. I didn’t want any of the blockchain grifts (especially not after the SEC told Telegram to stop it). I didn’t want NFT usernames. I didn’t want “gifts.” I don’t want to put in my birthday so that it can nag all my friends to buy me a “gift.” And I don’t want generative AI.

What I do want is a fast, secure, and reliable messenger application with stickers, end-to-end encryption, and attention to details like accessibility and power usage. Telegram isn’t fast any more, it’s less and less reliable, it still hasn’t made end-to-end encryption happen outside of secret chats, it’s a battery hog, and it frequently breaks VoiceOver. Oh, and I constantly get scam DMs from folks trying to convince me to send them money.

Signal has stickers now, and it has always been end-to-end encrypted. It’s a better choice than Telegram.

reviews.title: Getting hacked
reviews.text:
Over the past few weeks, I’ve noticed an alarming increase in reports of Telegram accounts being hacked, even when users are following normal and safe usage practices. This raises major concerns about the platform’s current security standards.

Despite being a widely used messaging app, Telegram seems to lack strong protection mechanisms such as robust login alerts, stricter verification steps, and more effective prevention against unauthorized access. Many users, including myself, do not feel adequately informed or safeguarded against potential breaches.

For an app that handles private conversations, personal files, and sensitive information, maintaining high-level security should be the top priority. Unfortunately, the recent experiences of multiple users indicate that there are significant vulnerabilities that need immediate attention from the development team.

I strongly urge the developers to investigate these issues, enhance account protection features, and provide clearer communication to users regarding security risks. Until these improvements are made, it is difficult to trust the app with personal data.
